title: Resident Evil 3 Was a Side Project. Code Veronica Was the Real Sequel
hook: Resident Evil 3 started life as a spin-off called Resident Evil 1.9, while the true follow-up to RE2 was Code Veronica on the Dreamcast. Which one deserves the number?
script: Did you know Resident Evil 3 was never supposed to be Resident Evil 3? In the late nineties, Capcom had a small side project in the works. Inside the studio it was known as Resident Evil one point nine. Director Kazuhiro Aoyama has said it was planned as a spin off, a short story about escaping Raccoon City. The real sequel to Resident Evil 2 was a different game entirely. That was Code Veronica, which Capcom was building for the Sega Dreamcast. Then the company changed its mind. The side project got a number, a new title, and a monster called Nemesis. Resident Evil 3 launched in Japan on September 22, 1999, and in America that November. It went on to sell about three and a half million copies. Code Veronica arrived a few months later, in early two thousand, with no number at all. Series creator Shinji Mikami was still thinking about it twenty years later. In a twenty twenty interview, he said the company asked his team to make it a numbered title. He also said Code Veronica deserved that number more. So the game with the three was the side project, and the real sequel went without one. Would you swap their names? Follow for more gaming history.
